chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from al-Husayn ibn Nu'aym, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who granted the residence of his house to another man for the days of his life, or made it for him and his descendants after him. He said: "It is for him and for his descendants according to what he stipulated."
I said: "If he needs to sell it, may he sell it?" He said: "Yes."

I said: "Does his sale of the house invalidate the right of residence?" He said: "The sale does not invalidate the right of residence. Thus did I hear my father عليه السلام say, Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: 'The sale does not invalidate the lease nor the residence, but he sells it on the condition that the one who buys it does not take ownership of what he bought until the residence ends according to what was stipulated, and likewise the lease.'"

I said: "If he returns to the tenant his money and all that he incurred in maintenance and repair regarding what he rented?" He said: "If it is with good pleasure of the soul and the tenant's consent to that, there is no harm."

key_terms.النَّفَقَةِ: expenses incurred in connection with the property
key_terms.الْبَيْعُ: the sale transaction of the property
key_terms.الْعِمَارَةِ: repair and maintenance of the property
key_terms.سُكْنَىٰ: the granted right of residence in a property
key_terms.شَرَطَ: stipulated as a condition in the agreement

ai.seo_question: Does selling a house cancel an existing right of residence or lease in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith explains rulings concerning a granted right of residence and lease in property transactions. It states that selling a property does not nullify an existing right of residence or ijarah, and any termination through repayment must be done with the tenant's willing consent.
